segments.text: Doctor, the tablets are not working. Still the room is spinning every time I turn in bed. I have not slept properly for days.
Okay, let's go through it step by step. When you say spinning, the room moves around you, or you feel unsteady?
The room moves, like a merry-go-round. It only lasts some seconds, maybe a minute, but it is so frightening. I hold the bed with both hands.
That sounds unpleasant. And when did this first begin?
About five weeks back. First I thought it was because of the heat, or low sugar, so I ate something and lay down, but it came again.
How often does it come now?
Every morning, when I turn on my side to get up. Sometimes also at night. Mostly when I turn to the right.
Mostly to the right, interesting. Does anything else bring it on, apart from turning in bed?
Looking up at the shelf in the kitchen. Yesterday I looked up for the salt box and I had to catch the counter.
And does anything make it settle, besides waiting?
Closing my eyes helps, and keeping still. That is all. Doctor, I saw a video on WhatsApp saying such things are from a brain tumour. Is it so?
Those forwarded videos cause more worry than they ever cure. Nothing you've told me so far points to something dangerous, but let's carry on with my questions.
Okay, okay. Please ask.
Any vomiting with the spinning?
No vomiting, only a little uneasy feeling in the stomach, and that passes.
Any ringing in your ears?
No, no ringing. My hearing is the same as always, my husband still says I don't listen, ha ha.
Ha, that's a universal complaint. Now, you came to see the other doctor two weeks ago, and he started something. What are you taking?
Betahistine, 16 mg, three times a day. He said it is for the dizziness.
And you've been taking it properly since then?
Yes, morning, afternoon and night, with food. I have not missed one, I even set an alarm on my phone.
Good, that's useful for me to know. Are you taking anything else, any other tablets or supplements?
No, only that one. Should I increase the dose? My neighbour says take double and it will work faster.
Please don't double anything on a neighbour's advice. Stay on the dose you have for now. It can take a few weeks to show its full effect.
A few weeks? But I am so scared to sleep, doctor. What if I fall and break something?
That's a very reasonable fear, and I'll give you some practical tips for it in a moment. First, tell me about your health in general. Any long-term conditions?
I get migraines sometimes, not often, maybe four times a year. And neck problem, cervical spondylosis, the X-ray was done long back, but I take no tablets for it.
All right, I'll note both of those down. Let me check your numbers now.
Blood pressure is 128 over 80, and your pulse is 74 beats per minute.
Is it okay? The last doctor said my pressure was a little high.
That's a perfectly good reading today. No need to worry about it.
Then why is the spinning happening? Can you tell me what it is?
I don't want to guess yet. What I'd like is to arrange a hearing and balance test, called audiometry, so we can see how the ears and balance system are working.
Is it a long test? I have to cook for my family when I reach home.
About forty minutes. You'll wear headphones and press a button when you hear a beep. The front desk can book you a slot this week.
Okay, I will do it. And in the meantime, what should I do about the falling thing?
Three simple things. Sit at the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand. Turn slowly rather than jerking over. And put a night light on the way to the bathroom.
Sit first, turn slowly, night light. I will write it down. My daughter will fix the light today only.
Perfect. And when you look up at the high shelf, get someone else to bring things down, so you're not tilting your head back.
Yes, I will ask my son to move the salt box lower, ha ha. It is always on the top shelf.
Ha, a simple fix. I'd like to see you again in three weeks, once the test is done, and we can look at everything together.
Three weeks. And if the spinning gets worse before that?
If you notice weakness in an arm or leg, trouble speaking, double vision or a severe headache, go to the emergency department straight away. Otherwise, continue as you are.
I will remember. Thank you, doctor. I was so scared, now I feel little bit calmer.
Good, that's what I wanted. Keep taking the tablets, and the best of luck with the cooking.
Thank you, doctor. Bye.
